# From grapple.nvim to mini.visits


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7906dda5-b1a7-499c-980b-c08f6ed5c6e0



I always thought it must be possible to use mini.visits in a similar way as `grapple` or `harpoon`

However, two previous implementation attempts failed.

In its **default** setup, `visits` has the following incompatible traits:

- Visits are created and updated automatically. The order is not under user-control.
- All visits are stored in the same file. When working in multiple simultaneous projects, the last project to close often overwrites other relevant visits.

Relevant line in help regarding simultaneous projects:

```txt
Notes:
- Storage is implemented in such a way that it doesn't really support more
  than one parallel Neovim processes. Meaning that if there are two or more
  simultaneous Neovim processes with same visit index storage path, the last
  one writing to it will preserve its visit history while others - won't.
```

Relevant line in help regarding harpoon:

```txt
... This module implements a more common labeling which does not imply order
with ability to make it automated depending on the task and/or preference ...
```

It took me a while to find the obvious solution: Store one index per project.
Having this basic approach, the rest of the implementation followed naturally.

**EDIT 20240822**: The latest version can be found [here](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/main/lua/ak/config/editor/mini_visits.lua) 

**EDIT 20240826**: 

I refactored the code into a separate internal plugin: [ak.mini.visits_harpooned](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/main/lua/ak/mini/visits_harpooned.lua) and [ak.mini.visits_harpooned_line](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/main/lua/ak/mini/visits_harpooned_line.lua)

## The setup

```lua
Visits.setup({
  list = { sort = H.sort }, -- only on recency
  silent = true, -- false,
  store = {
    autowrite = H.autowrite, -- if false, write on action
    normalize = H.gen_normalize(), -- remove visits without labels
    path = H.somewhat_unique_project_name(), -- store per project dir
  },
  track = { event = "" }, -- visits are added programmatically as a result of actions
})
```

This setup constrains the behaviour of `mini.visits`. I don't think it's possible to have the default experience alongside the functionality described in this post.
That said, I personally don't need default `mini.visits` functionality, as my workflow leans heavily on `grapple/harpoon` features, in combination with `mini.pick`, `oil` and `tmux`.

## Core version

**EDIT 20240819**: Added a standalone version without statusline and extra maintenance options.

<details>

<summary>core standalone version</summary>

```lua

-- Just a POC, showing the core setup needed to use mini.visits like grapple/harpoon.
-- Lacks a UI to add/remove/change files under label, but:
-- 1. Either clear the label from the files using a simple for loop.
-- 2. Add/remove a label on an individual file(toggle)
local Visits = require("mini.visits")

-- Helpers:
local H = {}

H.labels = { "main", "side", "test", "col" }
H.label = H.labels[1]
H.autowrite = false

H.map = function(lhs, rhs, desc) vim.keymap.set("n", lhs, rhs, { desc = desc, silent = true }) end

-- TODO: Good enough, but not guaranteed to be unique
H.somewhat_unique_project_name = function()
  local result = string.format("%s/%s", vim.fn.stdpath("data"), "mini-visits-index")
  local cwd = vim.fn.getcwd()
  local cwd_to_number = 1
  for i = 1, #cwd do -- transform cwd to a number
    cwd_to_number = cwd_to_number + string.byte(cwd, i)
  end
  return string.format("%s-%d-%s", result, cwd_to_number, vim.fn.fnamemodify(cwd, ":t"))
end

H.iterate = function(label, index) -- does not track!
  Visits.iterate_paths("first", nil, { filter = label, n_times = index })
end

H.sort = function(path_data_arr) -- only on recency
  table.sort(path_data_arr, function(a, b) return a.latest < b.latest end)
  return path_data_arr
end

H.gen_normalize = function() -- keep visits with labels, remove others
  local default = Visits.gen_normalize.default()
  return function(index)
    index = default(index)
    for cwd, paths in pairs(index) do
      for path, data in pairs(paths) do
        if not data.labels then index[cwd][path] = nil end
      end
    end
    return index
  end
end

H.on_change = function()
  if not H.autowrite then Visits.write_index() end
end

local A = { -- actions:
  ui = function() Visits.select_path(nil, { filter = H.label }) end,
  select = function(index) H.iterate(H.label, index) end,
  switch_context = function() -- alternatively: MiniExtra.pickers.visit_labels
    vim.ui.select(H.labels, { prompt = "Visits switch context" }, function(choice)
      if not choice then return end
      H.label = choice
    end)
  end,
  clear = function()
    local visits = Visits.list_paths(nil, { filter = H.label })
    for _, path in ipairs(visits) do
      Visits.remove_label(H.label, path)
    end
    H.on_change()
  end,
  toggle = function(label)
    local full_path = vim.fn.expand("%:p")
    if vim.list_contains(Visits.list_paths(nil, { filter = label }), full_path) then
      Visits.remove_label(label)
    else
      Visits.register_visit() -- must change "latest" field
      Visits.add_label(label)
    end
    H.on_change()
  end,
}

for _, key in ipairs({
  -- Most important keys:
  { "<leader>j", A.ui, desc = "Visits ui" },
  { "<leader>a", function() A.toggle(H.label) end, desc = "Visits toggle" },
  -- Open indexed file in current label:
  { "<c-j>", function() A.select(1) end, desc = "Visit 1" },
  { "<c-k>", function() A.select(2) end, desc = "Visit 2" },
  { "<c-l>", function() A.select(3) end, desc = "Visit 3" },
  { "<c-h>", function() A.select(4) end, desc = "Visit 4" },
  -- Other actions:
  { "<leader>oj", A.switch_context, desc = "Visits switch context" },
  { "<leader>or", A.clear, desc = "Visits clear" },
}) do
  H.map(key[1], key[2], key["desc"])
end

Visits.setup({
  list = { sort = H.sort }, -- only on recency
  silent = true, -- false,
  store = {
    autowrite = H.autowrite, -- if false, write on action
    normalize = H.gen_normalize(), -- remove visits without labels
    path = H.somewhat_unique_project_name(), -- store per project dir
  },
  track = { event = "" }, -- visits are added programmatically as a result of actions
})
```

</details>

## The code

All links are permalinks to fragments in my `Neovim` config: `https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde`

[`ak.config.editor.mini_visits`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/242a5eca715262e19b87a6a9c1bd59519b5a13a9/lua/ak/config/editor/mini_visits.lua#L245)

Covers the main part of the implementation. Contains 250 lines of code. Minus 100 lines for the "maintain dialogue" part, the resulting 150 lines compare nicely to the corresponding [grapple config.](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/editor/grapple.lua#L95)

~~Contains one [hack.](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/editor/mini_visits.lua#L121)
The hack is needed to change labeled visits in batch mode. By temporarily overriding `os.time`, each `latest` field in the visit will differ one second with the previous visit.~~

**EDIT 20240819**: Removed the hack. Not needed when using `MiniVisit.get_index()`. Updated permalink.

[`ak.config.ui.visitsline`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/ui/visitsline.lua#L74)

Show indicators for visits in the current context/label.
Used in [`ak.config.ui.mini_statusline.`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/ui/mini_statusline.lua#L174)
Corresponding `grapple` part: [`ak.config.ui.grappleline`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/ui/grappleline.lua#L71)

[`ak.config.editor.mini_pick`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/editor/mini_pick.lua#L221)

A customized picker to show all visits for all labels in the exact order per label.
Each line shows a label-path combination.
Key mapping: `<leader>,`

[`ak.config.editor.mini_pick_labeled`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/editor/mini_pick_labeled.lua#L12)

See [this discussion](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/1109)

Provides fast labels for all pickers(including `vim.ui.select`) that show `visit` information. Labels are just letters, as opposed to `labels` used in the context of `mini.visit`.

## Related code

[`ak.util.labels`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/util/labels.lua#L4)

Shared code defining the labels to use

[`ak.util.init`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/util/init.lua#L35)

Also label an `oil` buffer

[`ak.config.autocmds`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/config/autocmds.lua#L48)

Use `q` to close the "maintain" dialogue

[`ak.deps.editor`](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/df2a692a65badcac432aa60c8a082178f40207e3/lua/ak/deps/editor.lua#L49)

That's a nice project to craft what best suits your workflow!

At this level of complexity and incompatibility, though, maybe it would be better to write something own from scratch instead of forcing and hacking 'mini.visits'?

> At this level of complexity and incompatibility, though, maybe it would be better to write something own from scratch instead of forcing and hacking 'mini.visits'?

That's interesting...
At the same time you wrote the comment, I removed the hack. I updated the post accordingly.

Yes, the code I provided is complex. I removed the custom maintenance part and the statusline integration in order to show the core setup. This results in 100 lines of configuration, only using the options `mini.visits`( as part of the `mini` toolbox ) provides. 
Do you still think the following code snippet is complex and incompatible?

<details>
<summary>core version</summary>

```lua

-- Just a POC, showing the core setup needed to use mini.visits like grapple/harpoon.
-- Lacks a UI to add/remove/change files under label, but:
-- 1. Either clear the label from the files using a simple for loop.
-- 2. Add/remove a label on an individual file(toggle)
local Visits = require("mini.visits")

-- Helpers:
local H = {}

H.labels = { "main", "side", "test", "col" }
H.label = H.labels[1]
H.autowrite = false

H.map = function(lhs, rhs, desc) vim.keymap.set("n", lhs, rhs, { desc = desc, silent = true }) end

-- TODO: Good enough, but not guaranteed to be unique
H.somewhat_unique_project_name = function()
  local result = string.format("%s/%s", vim.fn.stdpath("data"), "mini-visits-index")
  local cwd = vim.fn.getcwd()
  local cwd_to_number = 1
  for i = 1, #cwd do -- transform cwd to a number
    cwd_to_number = cwd_to_number + string.byte(cwd, i)
  end
  return string.format("%s-%d-%s", result, cwd_to_number, vim.fn.fnamemodify(cwd, ":t"))
end

H.iterate = function(label, index) -- does not track!
  Visits.iterate_paths("first", nil, { filter = label, n_times = index })
end

H.sort = function(path_data_arr) -- only on recency
  table.sort(path_data_arr, function(a, b) return a.latest < b.latest end)
  return path_data_arr
end

H.gen_normalize = function() -- keep visits with labels, remove others
  local default = Visits.gen_normalize.default()
  return function(index)
    index = default(index)
    for cwd, paths in pairs(index) do
      for path, data in pairs(paths) do
        if not data.labels then index[cwd][path] = nil end
      end
    end
    return index
  end
end

H.on_change = function()
  if not H.autowrite then Visits.write_index() end
end

local A = { -- actions:
  ui = function() Visits.select_path(nil, { filter = H.label }) end,
  select = function(index) H.iterate(H.label, index) end,
  switch_context = function() -- alternatively: MiniExtra.pickers.visit_labels
    vim.ui.select(H.labels, { prompt = "Visits switch context" }, function(choice)
      if not choice then return end
      H.label = choice
    end)
  end,
  clear = function()
    local visits = Visits.list_paths(nil, { filter = H.label })
    for _, path in ipairs(visits) do
      Visits.remove_label(H.label, path)
    end
    H.on_change()
  end,
  toggle = function(label)
    local full_path = vim.fn.expand("%:p")
    if vim.list_contains(Visits.list_paths(nil, { filter = label }), full_path) then
      Visits.remove_label(label)
    else
      Visits.register_visit() -- must change "latest" field
      Visits.add_label(label)
    end
    H.on_change()
  end,
}

for _, key in ipairs({
  -- Most important keys:
  { "<leader>j", A.ui, desc = "Visits ui" },
  { "<leader>a", function() A.toggle(H.label) end, desc = "Visits toggle" },
  -- Open indexed file in current label:
  { "<c-j>", function() A.select(1) end, desc = "Visit 1" },
  { "<c-k>", function() A.select(2) end, desc = "Visit 2" },
  { "<c-l>", function() A.select(3) end, desc = "Visit 3" },
  { "<c-h>", function() A.select(4) end, desc = "Visit 4" },
  -- Other actions:
  { "<leader>oj", A.switch_context, desc = "Visits switch context" },
  { "<leader>or", A.clear, desc = "Visits clear" },
}) do
  H.map(key[1], key[2], key["desc"])
end

Visits.setup({
  list = { sort = H.sort }, -- only on recency
  silent = true, -- false,
  store = {
    autowrite = H.autowrite, -- if false, write on action
    normalize = H.gen_normalize(), -- remove visits without labels
    path = H.somewhat_unique_project_name(), -- store per project dir
  },
  track = { event = "" }, -- visits are added programmatically as a result of actions
})

```

</details>

I included the above fragment in the post as a separate chapter.

The statusline integration is handcrafted. The code started as a plugin for `harpoon`: [harpoonline](https://github.com/abeldekat/harpoonline).
When I moved to `grapple`, I archived `harpoonline` and simplified the code to be used in my config. It was trivial to copy the code to hook `mini.visits` into the `mini.statusline` component.

Naturally, there is a "fun" part at play. I could just as well keep using `grapple.nvim`.
However, when using `mini`, I get `mini.visits` for free. As in all components `mini` provides, the plugin is concise, stable, configurable and well tested. The plugin does a lot of the work I would otherwise need to code myself. I hope this is a valid argument against writing my own code from scratch...;)

reply_data.body:
You don't have to justify not wanting to write from scratch :) It was just an observation that came to mind while skimming through implementation. I am of course happy to see the proof that design of 'mini.nvim' modules is versatile enough to help implementing even vastly different workflows.

One thing I wanted to say several times, though. The core idea behind using `H` helper table is to be able to have code in "from top to bottom" order. Meaning that "main" functions go on top and helper go on bottom. This would be not possible with `local function ...` approach as they need to be defined before they are used in code. If you prefer using "from bottom to top" organization (which is totally fine), then using `local function` (or `local a = function()`) is a more convenient approach.

reply_data.body:
> ... The core idea behind using H helper table is to be able to have code in "from top to bottom" order...

Indeed. I do use this when there are lots of functions. There is another benefit, related to laziness: The order of the functions assigned to "H" does not matter...;). I am also thinking about code organization. I sometimes use an extra table, `A`, having functions related to actions.

Thanks for having a look at this post!
 
It's rewarding to be able to use a `mini` plugin for an important part in my workflow.
Also, the [pick_with_labels](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/1109) functionality is very useful in this part. Thanks again for helping me to create an implementation without hacks...;)
